label.trigger: A parent command holds a value for an option key that was stored through setOptionValue, or through setOptionValueWithSource called without a source, and a subcommand declares the same key which the user passes on its command line; code in the subcommand then asks for the merged source of that key.
label.expected_impact: The merged value returned by optsWithGlobals is the parent's, but the merged source lookup passes over the parent because its recorded source is undefined and reports the subcommand's 'cli'. A caller that branches on the source, for example to tell typed values from programmatic ones, gets a source that describes a different value than the one in effect.

context_locations.note: Plain value assignment goes through the source-recording setter with an empty source, so an entry whose source is undefined is an ordinary state rather than a missing one.
The merged values let an ancestor override the local value whenever it has the key at all; the source lookup is documented as the companion of this method and must pick the same command.
The published type lists undefined among the allowed source values, so storing it is part of the public contract and cannot serve as a not-present marker.

known_counterevidence.note: The chain lists the command first and its ancestors after it, so the overwrite order of the loop is right; a finding about traversal order does not match this defect, only the presence test does.

When every command in the chain recorded a string source such as default, env or cli, the merged source already agrees with the merged value; reports limited to default-value sources describe behaviour that works.

label.fix_summary: Treat a command in the chain as overriding when the key is present in its own source map (Object.hasOwn on _optionValueSources) instead of comparing the stored source with undefined, so an explicitly stored undefined source wins exactly as the value does.

check.summary: The upstream test file from the fix commit, run with the node test runner in TAP form; its new case stores a parent value without any source and expects the merged source lookup in the subcommand to give undefined.
check.failure_signature: not ok \d+ - when same named option used in sub CLI and program set value

verification.summary: verify --run-checks with node v24.18.0: on before the added test case reports 'not ok' (merged source is 'cli' instead of undefined) and the runner exits non-zero; on after every test in the file passes. The package has no runtime dependencies and nothing is installed. Three test fixture symlinks under tests/fixtures are not written to the trees; the check does not use them.
